name: root
tooltip: A placeholder for the root of the classification tree.

children.name: Accidental
children.tooltip: Accidental/spontaneous integration events.

children.name: Normally_Non-integrating_Virus
children.tooltip: Virus families that are more likely the result of spontaneous integration rather than Retrotranposition.

children.name: Artifact
children.tooltip: Elements often found in cloning vectors that may contaminate sequencing projects.

children.name: Interspersed_Repeat
children.tooltip: A repetitive sequence with copies interspersed throughout an organisms genome.

children.name: Pseudogene
children.tooltip: Duplications of existing genes in an organism.

children.name: RNA
children.tooltip: Non-translated, small RNA genes often found in high copy number.

children.name: rRNA
children.tooltip: Copies of a ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene or pseudogene.

children.name: snRNA
children.tooltip: Copies of a small nuclear RNA (snRNA) gene or pseudogene.
children.description: Small nuclear RNAs include 7SK RNA and the U1 to U13. They are dependent on external promoters and are theferore much less frequently involved in the creation of a SINE

children.name: tRNA
children.tooltip: Copies of a transfer RNA (tRNA) gene or pseudogene.
children.description: In mammals,  tRNAs copies can occur in relatively large numbers (up to a thousand copies) The boundary between a large number of accidentally retroposed or otherwise duplicated (pseudo)genes and a low copy number SINE (selected on its ability to propagate) is nebulous

children.name: Transposable_Element
children.tooltip: Families that are the direct result of transposition events.

children.name: Class_II_DNA_Transposition
children.tooltip: Elements that do not require an RNA intermediate in their transposition lifecycle.

children.name: Casposon
children.tooltip: Archaeal and bacterial mobile elements at the origin of CRISPR-Cas immunity.

children.name: Helicase
children.tooltip: Circular ssDNA Intermediate.

children.name: Transposase
children.tooltip: DNA transposons with terminal inverted repeats ranging from 6 bp to many kb.
children.description: Autonomous elements have a DD(E/D) transposase. Most DNA transposons fall in this class. Some non-autonomous elements, hairpin

children.name: Academ
children.tooltip: Academ superfamily of  DNA transposons.
children.description: Found in metazoans and fungi, autonomous Academ elements encode a ca 1.5 kb protein containing an XPG exonuclease domain, a Cys8 zinc finger, and a DDE transposase domain unlike those of others. Termini tend to be TAGÃCTA and a 3 bp target site is duplicated.

children.name: Academ-1
children.tooltip: First described family of Academ DNA transposon.

children.name: Academ-2
children.tooltip: Second described family of Academ DNA transposon.

children.name: Academ-H
children.tooltip: Family of Academ transposons described in rust fungi.

children.name: CACTA
children.tooltip: A group of DNA transposons with characteristic CACTAâ¦TAGTG termini.

children.name: CMC
children.tooltip: CACTA (EnSpm), Mirage, Chapaev group with related DNA transposons.

children.name: Chapaev_group
children.tooltip: Superfamily including  Chapaev and Chapaev-3 elements.

children.name: Chapaev
children.tooltip: So-far animal-specific elements with a specific DDE transposase.

children.name: Chapaev-3
children.tooltip: So-far animal-specific elements with a specific DDE transposase.

children.name: Transib
children.tooltip: Group of DNA transposons at the basis of our adaptive immune system.

children.name: Mutator-like
children.tooltip: Mutator-like Element aka MULE.

children.name: Ant1
children.tooltip: A group of DNA transposons so far limited to fungi.

children.name: Tc2-group
children.tooltip: Containing the sister clades of Tc2, Pogo, Fot1, and Tigger DNA transposons.

children.name: Tigger
children.tooltip: So far animal-specific mariner-like elements with the mammalian Tigger1 as type specimen.

children.name: hAT
children.tooltip: hobo Activator Tam3 Elements.

children.name: Activator
children.tooltip: A large class in plants and animals named after the maize element.

children.name: Blackjack
children.tooltip: A group of hAT transposons possibly closest to Charlie elements.

children.name: Charlie
children.tooltip: Mostly animal-specific hAT transposons with the mammalian Charlie1 as type specimen.

children.name: Tip100
children.tooltip: Widespread class of hAT elements, including the Arthur and Zaphod elements in ancient mammals.

children.name: Class_I_Retrotransposition
children.tooltip: Elements that require an RNA intermediate in their transposition lifecycle.

children.name: LINE
children.tooltip: Long Interspersed Nuclear Element.

children.name: Group-I
children.tooltip: Based on reverse transcriptase phylogeny, an outlier group containing the Ambal, CRE and Odin LINE elements.

children.name: Ambal
children.tooltip: A group of LINE  so far specific to Diatoms.

children.name: Group-II
children.tooltip: The bulk of the LINE elements.

children.name: Group-1
children.tooltip: Containing the sister classes of Proto-1, L1-like, R2-like, and R4-like LINE elements.

children.name: L1-like
children.tooltip: Containing the sister classes of DRE, L1, Tx1, and Zorro LINE elements.

children.name: L1-group
children.tooltip: Containing the closely related L1 and Tx1 LINE elements.

children.name: L1
children.tooltip: A large group of LINE elements with mammalian LINE-1 (L1) as type specimen.

children.name: R2-like
children.tooltip: Containing the sister clades of R2, Hero and NeSL LINEs.

children.name: R4-like
children.tooltip: Containing the sister clades of Deceiver, Dong-R4, and Dualen LINE elements.

children.name: Group-2
children.tooltip: Containing the sister classes of Proto-2, R1-like, and RTE-like LINE elements.

children.name: R1-like
children.tooltip: Containing Tad1, CR1-related and R1-related LINEs.

children.name: CR1-group
children.tooltip: Containing the sister classes of CR1, L2 and Rex-Babar LINEs.

children.name: CR1
children.tooltip: A large group of LINE elements with Chicken Repeat 1 (CR1) as type specimen.

children.name: L2-group
children.tooltip: A large group of L2-like elements that can still need to be subclassified.

children.name: L2
children.tooltip: A large group of LINE elements with mammalian LINE-2 (L2) as type specimen.

children.name: R1-group

children.name: I-group

children.name: R1-subgroup
children.tooltip: Containing the closely related LOA and R1 LINEs.

children.name: BovB

children.tooltip: Nonautonomous retroposons derived from I-type LINEs.

children.name: SINE
children.tooltip: Short LINE-dependent retroposons with an internal (usually pol III) promoter.
children.description: The median length of described SINEs is ca. 250 bp Â±130 bp SD. The canonical SINE has a tRNA 5' end with the internal promoter, a core of unknown function shared with multiple other SINE families, a 3' end identical to that of the LINE responsible for its mobility, and a simple repeat tail. A few SINEs have a LINE-derived internal pol II promoter, and many lack either or both the core and LINE-derived regions.
